## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag needs to read its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, because the project's cli-flags policy requires this for every new flag under `cli/`. Without it, CI cannot set exclusions through the environment.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` option. `collect` uses it to skip any file whose basename matches one of the patterns, and it logs each skipped path. The change also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds parser, `collect` and end-to-end archive tests.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Default `--exclude` from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — `--exclude` is a new flag under `cli/`, but its default is the literal `default=[]`, so setting `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` has no effect. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot exclude files, so their archives still contain the files they meant to leave out. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, decide on a separator for multiple patterns, update the Default column at `docs/flags.md:7`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` to cover the environment variable.
